in_hebrew.name: קריסטופור
in_hebrew.meaning: נושא את המשיח, הוביל את המשיח
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קריסטופור מקורו במילים 'Χριστός' (המשיח) ו'φορέω' (לשאת, להוביל). הוא נגזר מהשורש העברי 'מָשִׁיחַ' (משיח) ומשמעותו 'נושא את המשיח' או 'הוביל את המשיח'. השם משקף את הדמות הנוצרית של נושא המשיח או מוביל את דרכו של המשיח.

in_greek.name: Χριστόφορος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Χριστόφορος προέρχεται από το 'Χριστός' (Christ) και 'φορέω' (να φέρω, να κουβάλω). Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα αντανακλά την πνευματική σχέση του ονοματοθετούμένου με τον Ιησού Χριστό, ως αυτός που φέρνει ή οδηγεί τον Χριστό. Είναι χαρακτηριστικό των ονομάτων που συνδέονται με την Ορθοδοξία και την πίστη στην Αγία Τριάδα.

in_latin.name: Christophorus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Christophorus derivatur a 'Christus' et 'fero', quod significat 'Christum ferens' vel 'Christum gerens'. Hoc nomen christianum exprimebat fidem et devotionem ad Iesum Christum, quasi is qui Christum in corde suo gestat et vitam suam ad eius exemplo informat.

in_english.name: Kristofor
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kristofor originates from the Greek words 'Χριστός' (Christ) and 'φορέω' (to bear or carry). It signifies one who bears or carries Christ, reflecting a deep spiritual connection with Jesus Christ. Historically, the name has been used in Christian traditions to denote a follower of Christ or someone who leads others in the path of Christ. The name is associated with Saint Christopher, a 3rd-century martyr and one of the most popular saints in Christian tradition, known as the patron saint of travelers.

biblical_reference.note: Though not directly mentioned in the Bible, the name reflects New Testament themes.

saint_reference.note: Patron saint of travelers, protector against harm while journeying.

data.cultural_impact: Kristofor was a popular name among early Christians in Europe, particularly among the Slavic peoples. The name is believed to have originated from the Greek word 'Christos', which means 'Anointed One', and 'Philos', meaning 'Lover of'. This name acknowledged the Christian belief that Jesus Christ was the Anointed One, sent by God to save humanity from sin, and the lofty ideal of a Christian - to be a lover of Christ and His teachings.
data.spiritual_significance: Kristofor is a name deeply rooted in Christian spirituality and symbolism. It serves as a reminder of the significance of Christ in the lives of believers and the importance of emulating His love, compassion, and kindness in our daily interactions with others.

historical_references.reference: Born in Byzantium around 1350, Kristofor was a renowned explorer and cartographer who discovered the northern sea route to India.
